hints.title: Position-Targeted Line Extraction
hints.text: A specific line number must be retrieved from a text file, producing no output if the file contains fewer lines. How can a text utility extract exactly one target line index without redundant scanning?

hints.title: Stream Editing Address Printing
hints.text: Stream editors allow addressing individual line numbers directly, suppressing default output and selectively printing only the addressed line.

hints.title: Sed Targeted Print Command
hints.text: Run sed with the -n flag to suppress default printing, and supply the script 10p pointing to file.txt. If the file has 10 or more lines, line 10 is printed. If it contains fewer, no output is emitted.

variables: N: number of lines in file.txt
complexity.notes: Streaming single-pass line inspection with early exit capability.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Slurping the entire file into memory with cat file.txt | head -n 10 | tail -n 1 spawns multiple pipeline processes and consumes buffer memory proportional to file size, failing or slowing down when files have fewer than 10 lines.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: sed -n '10p' file.txt streams line-by-line using O(1) constant buffer space and prints only line 10, executing in O(N) streaming time (or early-exiting with 10q on large files).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling files with fewer than 10 lines cleanly (must output nothing); avoiding multiple spawned subshells when a single stream editor tool suffices.

solutions.approach: Sed Stream Addressing with Suppressed Default Print
